chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath, from his father
That Ali (peace be upon him) would detain a debtor in debt; but when insolvency and need became clear to him, he would release his path (allow him freedom to work) until he acquired wealth.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali handle debtors who were unable to pay?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the juristic principle of *al-‘Iqrar bi al-Insaf* (fairness in debt), where Imam Ali (AS) balanced the creditor's right with the debtor's capacity to pay. By releasing the insolvent debtor to earn a living, he prioritized practical solvency over punitive detention, a precedent often cited in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between mere delay and true insolvency (*al-‘Irsal*).
